newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe industrial stocks end firm.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe industrial stocks end firm.

text.p: Zimbabwean industrial stocks traded predictably firmer on Thursday in a market which many analysts expect to continue on a largely strong course for some weeks on local investor sentiment.

"Share demand may actually rise in coming days as some investors move from the (Zimbabwe) money market to stocks," one broker said of the money market where short-term interest rates have fallen to around 20 percent from 30 percent in January, and are seen staying lower for a while on high liquidity.
"But (share) volumes may remain low because sellers are likely to thin out as we approach the holidays," he added.
On Thursday, the key 57-share industrial index surged 129 points to close at 8,209.71 on the back of some agriculture-based companies and two bluechips.

Sugar producer Hippo Valley, Zimbabwe Sugar Refinery (ZSR) and seed company Seed-Co traded 20 cents higher each at 960, 1,400 and 240. Heavyweights, conglomerate Delta and hotel group Zimsun, traded 100 cents higher at 3,500 and 20 cents at 400.

Investor interest in some of these industrial shares has risen considerably in the past month on predictions that current good rains may see the southern African country's agriculture-driven economy growing by up to seven percent in 1997 from an estimated five percent this year.

The Zimbabwe Stock Exchange's secondary seven-counter mining index plunged 130.85 points to 1,065.76, dragged lower by gold miners Rio Tinto, which dropped 200 cents to 3,000, and nickel producer Bindura, which slipped 20 cents to 820.
Brokers said Zimbabwe minings traditionally do not enjoy investor support this time of the year.
"The dominant players are corporates who tend to hold back around the festive season and have their attention on industrials," one said.
